title_ar: النصاب الذي تصح به صلاة الجمعة
title_en: The Quorum by Which the Friday Prayer Is Valid
body_ar:
قرية فيها جامع وإمامها يصلي الجمعة إذا تم له اثنى عشر رجلا وإلا تركها وصلاها ظهرا فهل هذا فعل صحيح أم لا؟

أن عدد الرجال الذين تجب بهم الجمعة لم يرد فيه تحديد من الشرع إلا ما أخرج مسلم في الصحيح من حديث أبي سعيد الخدري أن رسول الله (ص) قال: «إذا كانوا ثلاثة فليؤمهم أحدهم» وقد قال العلامة عبد الحق الإشبيلي رحمه الله وهو من كبار علماء المالكية، قال: هذا عام في الجمعة وفي غيرها لا مخصص له من الشرع، فعلى هذا النصاب الذي تصلى به الجمعة وغيرها من الصلوات هو ثلاثة رجال هذا الذي ثبت عن النبي (ص)..

أما اثنى عشر رجلا فقد بقوا مع النبي (ص) يوم العير، ولم يمسكهم هو ولم يأمرهم بل كان ذلك قدرا فقط، والقدر لا يحتج به، فالخطاب بالشرع لا بالقدر، التكليف كله بالشرع لا بالقدر، وليس من شروط الجمعة الأمن ولا السوق ولا نحو ذلك فقد صلى النبي (ص) الجمعة في أيام الحصار في أيام الأحزاب، وكانت المدينة أشد خوفا من أي مكان آخر إذ ذاك، وقد بين الله حالة أهلها فقال: {إِذْ جَاءُوكُمْ مِنْ فَوْقِكُمْ وَمِنْ أَسْفَلَ مِنْكُمْ وَإِذْ زَاغَتِ الْأَبْصَارُ وَبَلَغَتِ الْقُلُوبُ الْحَنَاجِرَ وَتَظُنُّونَ بِاللَّهِ الظُّنُونَا (10) هُنَالِكَ ابْتُلِيَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَزُلْزِلُوا زِلْزَالًا شَدِيدًا (11)} [الأحزاب] وهذا الحال من الخوف إذا كان حاصلا فلا يمكن أن يكون حال أهل قرية أخرى مثل هذا الحال، إذا كان هذا لم يكن عذرا في ترك الجمعة فإنما يتذرع الناس بذلك من عمل الشيطان فقط.
body_en:
A village that has a congregational mosque, whose imam prays the Friday prayer when twelve men are complete for him, and otherwise leaves it and prays it as the noon prayer — is this a correct practice or not?

The number of men by whom the Friday prayer becomes obligatory has no delimitation laid down for it in the revealed law, except for what Muslim brought out in the Sahih from the hadith of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'When they are three, let one of them lead them.' And the erudite ʿAbd al-Haqq al-Ishbili, God have mercy on him — who is among the great scholars of the Malikis — said: this is general, covering the Friday prayer and others, and there is nothing in the revealed law to specify it. So on this basis, the quorum (niṣāb) by which the Friday prayer and the other prayers are prayed is three men. This is what is established from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him..

As for twelve men: they remained with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, on the day of the caravan, and he did not hold them back and did not command them; rather that was merely how it fell out, and how a thing falls out is not used as an argument. For the address of the revealed law is by the law, not by how things fall out; the whole of legal obligation is by the law, not by how things fall out. And it is not among the conditions of the Friday prayer that there be security, nor a market, nor anything of the kind, for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed the Friday prayer in the days of the siege, in the days of the Confederates, and Medina was at that time in more intense fear than any other place. God has set out the state of its people, saying: {When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when eyes swerved and hearts reached the throats, and you were thinking thoughts about God. There the believers were tried, and shaken with a severe shaking} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:10–11). And this state of fear, when it actually obtained — it cannot be that the state of the people of some other village is like this state. If this was not an excuse for abandoning the Friday prayer, then people's making a pretext of that is merely the work of Satan.

flags.arabic: فعلى هذا النصاب الذي تصلى به الجمعة وغيرها من الصلوات هو ثلاثة رجال
flags.context: the Sheikh's own ruling on the quorum
options: render literally, keeping the chain of reasoning that leads to it
render as a permission rather than a ruling
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW — THIS RULING DEPARTS FROM THE STANDARD POSITION OF HIS OWN SCHOOL. The well-known Maliki position requires twelve men for the Friday prayer, which is precisely what the village imam in the question is doing. The Sheikh rules for three, and he gets there by a usul argument: no delimitation exists in the law; the only relevant text is general; and there is nothing to specify it. He supports this by citing a Maliki authority, ʿAbd al-Haqq al-Ishbili, rather than by setting himself against the school. The reasoning chain must be preserved and not compressed into its conclusion, and the ruling must not be presented as simply 'the Maliki position'. Given that it changes practice in village mosques, the publication decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.context: the term in the title and in the ruling
flags.note: IMPORTANT — A GLOSSARY TERM IN A DIFFERENT SENSE. The glossary fixes niṣāb as 'the minimum threshold' in the zakat sense. Here it means the quorum of worshippers required for a valid congregational Friday prayer, which is a different technical use of the same word. Using the glossary's zakat rendering would be actively misleading. The second sense should be recorded in the glossary.

flags.arabic: بل كان ذلك قدرا فقط، والقدر لا يحتج به، فالخطاب بالشرع لا بالقدر
flags.context: the Sheikh's rebuttal of the argument from the twelve men
options: render qadar as 'how it fell out' / 'how a thing falls out', as done here
flags.note: A TERM THAT MUST NOT BE READ IN ITS CREEDAL SENSE HERE. qadar in records 553, 561 and 563 of this slice is the sixth article of faith, the divine decree. Here it is being used in the usul sense of what merely happened to be the case, as opposed to what the law addresses and requires — the Sheikh's whole point is that the number twelve is a fact about one occasion, not a legal stipulation. Rendering it 'divine decree' would make the sentence incoherent, and 'coincidence' would deny the theological sense he does not intend to deny. The paraphrase used here is unavoidably loose and a reviewer should settle the rendering; qadar is in any case on the style guide's pending list (§13).

flags.context: the occasion on which twelve men remained with the Prophet
options: the day of the trade caravan
flags.note: This refers to the occasion behind Sūrat al-Jumuʿah 62:11, when a trading caravan arrived during the Friday sermon and the congregation left for it. The Sheikh does not explain the reference or cite the verse, assuming his listeners know it, and nothing has been supplied. An English reader will not know it; a reviewer should decide whether the site glosses it, since the whole rebuttal depends on the reader knowing what happened.

flags.arabic: وليس من شروط الجمعة الأمن ولا السوق
flags.context: the conditions the Sheikh rules out
options: it is not among the conditions of the Friday prayer that there be security, nor a market
safety and a marketplace are not prerequisites for the Friday prayer
neither public order nor a market is required
flags.note: EDITORIAL NOTE. This clause rules that insecurity is not an excuse for suspending the Friday prayer, and the record closes by calling the invocation of such excuses the work of Satan. In a setting where congregational prayer may be curtailed for stated security reasons, that has an obvious edge, and it should be read alongside record 598 of this slice, where the Sheikh rules that the civil authority's permission is not required for the Friday prayer. Both have been translated faithfully and neither has been softened. 'Conditions' renders shurūṭ per the glossary.

Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The source writes the eulogy after the Prophet's name sometimes in full and sometimes as the abbreviation (ص). Both are rendered as 'peace and blessings be upon him'; the source form is preserved in body_ar.

The Qur'anic quotation carries its sūrah name in square brackets and its verse numbers in the source; the reference has been rendered per house style. The source spells الظُّنُونَا with the final alif, as the ʿuthmānī orthography has it.

'This is general … and there is nothing in the revealed law to specify it' renders ʿāmm … lā mukhaṣṣiṣa lahu min al-sharʿ, the technical usul vocabulary of the general and the specifying text; the glossary entries for ʿāmm and khāṣṣ apply.
The source writes اثنى عشر for اثني عشر in both places; preserved in body_ar.
The double full stop after 'established from the Prophet' is in the source and does not here mark a break in the text, since the answer continues; preserved in body_ar.
